openkeyscan_source.note: Pinned commit (upstream has no tags). Read for PREPROCESSING.md on 2026-11-04.

export.parity: PyTorch vs ORT CPU max |dlogits| < 1e-4 (measured 1.43e-06 on the 5 fixtures)

openkeyscan3_onnx.note: sha256 identifies the reference export (made on the dev machine). Exports are NOT byte-reproducible across machines: onnxsim folds constants with CPU-specific ONNX Runtime kernels (a GitHub Linux x86-64 runner produced a7a57a41..., same pins, same parity). The app and tools/models.py therefore also accept any export whose openkeyscan3.onnx.provenance.json (written by ml/export_openkeyscan.py) matches the file and records a passing parity check against the pinned commit + checkpoint. url stays null until a file is hosted somewhere we control.

openkeyscan_sidecar.phase: A (M1 only; removed in M2, see packaging-and-release M2 removal checklist)
openkeyscan_sidecar.artifacts_note: url/sha256 stay null until a built zip is published somewhere we control (or an upstream release asset is pinned). `make models` then downloads + verifies; until then it uses the zip produced by the build script.

htdemucs_pt.name: htdemucs
htdemucs_pt.note: Single model (bag of 1, weights 1). Fetched by demucs.pretrained.get_model into the torch hub cache.

export.parity: upstream forward vs istft(ORT spec_out) + ORT wave_out, max |d| < 1e-3 (measured 4.8e-04 / SNR >= 83 dB on house, pop, techno)

htdemucs_onnx.note: Network core only: STFT/ISTFT, normalisation and segmenting are done in C++ (engine/stems). sha256 identifies the reference export (Linux x86-64 dev machine); like openkeyscan3, other machines produce other bytes and are accepted via htdemucs.onnx.provenance.json. 174 MB: never bundled, exported or downloaded into the models dir.
